The nine camps of the Yaolian were made nine meng'an subordinate to it; together with the Upper Capital and Taizhou, six offices were established in all, each commanding fifty or sixty thousand men; the Bohai army was also made eight meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Xi were not yet pacified, a Xi Route Chief Command Bureau was also established, later renamed the Six Departments Route Chief Command Bureau. The nine camps of the Yaolian became nine subordinate meng'an; together with offices at the Upper Capital and Taizhou, six bureaus were established in all, each commanding fifty or sixty thousand men, and the Bohai army was organized into eight meng'an.

sentences.zh: 凡猛安之上置軍帥，軍帥之上置萬戶，萬戶之上置都統。

translations.literal: Above each meng'an an army marshal was placed; above the army marshal a wanhu; above the wanhu a chief commander.
translations.idiomatic: Above each meng'an stood an army marshal; above the army marshal a wanhu; above the wanhu a chief commander.

sentences.zh: 然時亦稱軍帥為猛安，而猛安則稱親管猛安者。

translations.literal: Yet at the time the army marshal was also called meng'an, while meng'an was called personally commanded meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, however, army marshals were also called meng'an, while meng'an in the strict sense denoted a personally commanded meng'an.

sentences.zh: 燕山既下，循遼制立樞密院于廣寧府，以總漢軍。

translations.literal: Once Yan Mountain was taken, following Liao practice a Privy Council was established at Guangning Prefecture to command the Han armies.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan Mountain fell, the Jin followed Liao practice and established a Privy Council at Guangning Prefecture to command the Han armies.

sentences.zh: 太宗天會元年，以襲遼主所立西南都統府為西南、西北兩路都統府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianhui under Emperor Taizong, the Southwest Chief Command Office established when the Liao ruler was attacked became the Southwest and Northwest Route Chief Command Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianhui under Emperor Taizong, the Southwest Chief Command Office created during the attack on the Liao ruler was split into Southwest and Northwest Route Chief Command Offices.

sentences.zh: 三年，以伐宋更為元帥府，置元帥及左、右副，及左、右監軍，左、右都監。

translations.literal: In the third year, because of the campaign against Song it was changed to a Marshal Prefecture, with a marshal, left and right deputies, left and right supervising generals, and left and right chief supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, with war against Song underway, the office was converted into a Marshal Prefecture, with a marshal, left and right deputies, left and right supervising generals, and left and right chief supervisors.

sentences.zh: 金制，都元帥必以諳版孛極烈為之，恆居守而不出。

translations.literal: Under Jin institutions, the chief marshal was invariably an apan begile, who always remained on guard and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin practice the chief marshal was always an apan begile, who remained on guard at court and did not take the field.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔還二帥以鎮方面。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, an edict ordered the two marshals to return and guard the regions.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year an edict recalled the two marshals to guard their respective regions.

sentences.zh: 諸路各設兵馬都總管府，州鎮置節度使，沿邊州則置防禦使。

translations.literal: Each route established a Cavalry and Infantry Chief Command Prefecture; prefectures and garrison towns had military commissioners, and frontier prefectures had defense commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Each circuit established a Cavalry and Infantry Chief Command Prefecture; prefectures and garrison towns received military commissioners, and frontier prefectures defense commissioners.

sentences.zh: 凡州府所募射糧軍、牢城軍，每五百人為一指揮使司，設使，分為四都，都設左右什將及承局押官。

translations.literal: As for grain-supply archers and Prison-City troops recruited by prefectures and prefectural cities, every five hundred men formed one commandant's office with a commander, divided into four companies; each company had left and right squad leaders and clerks as supervising officers.
translations.idiomatic: Grain-supply archers and Prison-City troops recruited by prefectures and prefectural cities were organized with five hundred men to a commandant's office under a commander, divided into four companies; each company had left and right squad leaders and clerks as supervising officers.

sentences.zh: 其軍數若有餘或不足，則與近者合置，不可合者以三百人或二百人亦設指揮使，若百人則止設軍使，百人以上立為都，不及百人止設什將及承局管押官各一員。

translations.literal: If troop numbers were surplus or insufficient, they were combined with nearby units; where combination was impossible, three hundred or two hundred men also had a commander established; if one hundred men, only an army commander was established; if over one hundred men a company was formed, and if under one hundred men only one squad leader and one clerk-supervisor were established.
translations.idiomatic: Where numbers exceeded or fell short of five hundred, units were combined with neighboring ones; where combination was impossible, commands of three hundred or two hundred were also permitted. A force of one hundred had only an army commander; above one hundred a company was formed; below one hundred only a squad leader and a clerk-supervisor were appointed.

sentences.zh: 十年，改南京路都統司為東南路都統司，治東京以鎮高麗。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the Southern Capital Route Chief Command Bureau was changed to the Southeast Route Chief Command Bureau, administering the Eastern Capital to guard Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the Southern Capital Route Chief Command Bureau was renamed the Southeast Route Chief Command Bureau, based at the Eastern Capital to guard against Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 後又置統軍司於大名府。

translations.literal: Later a Commanding Army Bureau was also established at Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later a Commanding Army Bureau was also established at Daming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及海陵天德二年八月，改諸京兵馬都部署司為本路都總管府。

translations.literal: By the eighth month of the second year of Tiande under Hailing, the Cavalry and Infantry Chief Deployment Offices of the various capitals were changed to route chief command prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of Tiande under Hailing, the Cavalry and Infantry Chief Deployment Offices of the various capitals were converted into route chief command prefectures.

sentences.zh: 九月，罷大名統軍司，而置統軍司于山西、河南、陝西三路。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Daming Commanding Army Bureau was abolished, and Commanding Army Bureaus were established in the Shanxi, Henan, and Shaanxi routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Daming Commanding Army Bureau was abolished and Commanding Army Bureaus were established in the Shanxi, Henan, and Shaanxi circuits.

sentences.zh: 以元帥府都監、監軍為使，分統天下之兵。

translations.literal: The chief supervisors and supervising generals of the Marshal Prefecture served as commissioners, dividing command of the realm's armies.
translations.idiomatic: Chief supervisors and supervising generals of the Marshal Prefecture served as commissioners, dividing command of the empire's armies.

sentences.zh: 又改烏古迪烈路統軍司為招討司，以婆速路統軍司為總管府。

translations.literal: The Ugu Dilie Route Commanding Army Bureau was also changed to a Pacification Bureau, and the Posu Route Commanding Army Bureau to a Chief Command Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Ugu Dilie Route Commanding Army Bureau was also converted into a Pacification Bureau, and the Posu Route Commanding Army Bureau into a Chief Command Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三年，以元帥府為樞密院，罷萬戶之官，詔曰：「太祖開創，因時制宜，材堪統眾授之萬戶，其次千戶及謀克。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Marshal Prefecture became the Privy Council and the office of wanhu was abolished. The edict said: "Taizu at the founding, adapting to the times, granted the title wanhu to those whose talent could command the multitude; next came qianhu and mouke.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Marshal Prefecture became the Privy Council and the office of wanhu was abolished. The edict read: "At the founding Taizu adapted institutions to the times and granted the title wanhu to men capable of commanding large forces; below them came qianhu and mouke.

sentences.zh: 當時官賞未定，城郭未下，設此職許以世襲，乃權宜之制，非經久之利。

translations.literal: At that time offices and rewards were not yet fixed, city walls were not yet taken; establishing these posts and permitting hereditary succession was an expedient measure, not a lasting benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Offices and rewards were not yet fixed and cities had not yet fallen; creating these posts with hereditary succession was an expedient, not a permanent institution.

sentences.zh: 今子孫相繼專攬威權，其戶不下數萬，與留守總管無異，而世權過之。

translations.literal: Now descendants succeed one another and monopolize military authority; their households number no less than tens of thousands, no different from garrison commanders and chief prefects, yet their hereditary power exceeds them.
translations.idiomatic: Now their descendants succeed one another and monopolize military authority; their households number in the tens of thousands, equal to garrison commanders and chief prefects, yet their hereditary power exceeds even those offices.

sentences.zh: 可罷是官。

translations.literal: This office may be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: This office shall be abolished.

sentences.zh: 若舊無千戶之職者，續思增置。

translations.literal: Where there was formerly no qianhu post, consideration shall be given to adding one.
translations.idiomatic: Where no qianhu post previously existed, the court shall consider establishing one.

sentences.zh: 國初時賜以國姓，若為子孫者皆令復舊。

translations.literal: Those granted the dynastic surname at the founding—if they became descendants—are all ordered to revert to their original surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Those granted the dynastic surname at the founding shall, they and their descendants, revert to their original surnames.

sentences.zh: 」正隆末，複升陝西統軍司為都統府。

translations.literal: " At the end of Zhenglong, the Shaanxi Commanding Army Bureau was again elevated to a Chief Command Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " At the end of Zhenglong the Shaanxi Commanding Army Bureau was again elevated to a Chief Command Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大定五年，複罷府，降為統軍司。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dading, the prefecture was again abolished and reduced to a Commanding Army Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Dading the prefecture was again abolished and reduced to a Commanding Army Bureau.

sentences.zh: 尋又設兩招討司，與前凡三，以鎮邊陲。

translations.literal: Soon two Pacification Bureaus were also established; with those before, three in all, to guard the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Soon two more Pacification Bureaus were established, making three in all to guard the frontier.

sentences.zh: 東北路者，初置烏古迪烈部，後置於泰州。

translations.literal: The Northeast Route: first established in the Ugu Dilie division, later placed at Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Northeast Route was first established in the Ugu Dilie division and later moved to Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 泰和間，以去邊尚三百里，宗浩乃命分司於金山。

translations.literal: During Taihe, because it was still three hundred li from the border, Zonghao ordered a branch office at Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: During Taihe, because the office lay three hundred li from the frontier, Zonghao ordered a branch established at Jinshan.

sentences.zh: 西北路者置於應州，西南路者置於桓州，以重臣知兵者為使，列城堡濠牆，戍守為永制。

translations.literal: The Northwest Route was placed at Yingzhou and the Southwest Route at Huanzhou; eminent ministers versed in military affairs served as commissioners, arranging castles, walls, and moats, with garrison duty as a permanent system.
translations.idiomatic: The Northwest Route was based at Yingzhou and the Southwest Route at Huanzhou; senior ministers experienced in military affairs served as commissioners, building castles, walls, and moats under a permanent garrison system.

sentences.zh: 樞密院每行兵則更為元帥府，罷則複為院。

translations.literal: Whenever the Privy Council took the field it was again changed to a Marshal Prefecture; when campaigns ended it reverted to a bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Privy Council took the field it was temporarily converted into a Marshal Prefecture; when campaigns ended it reverted to a bureau.

sentences.zh: 宣宗貞祐三年，征代州戍兵五千，從胥鼎言，留代以屏平陽。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyou under Emperor Xuanzong, five thousand garrison troops of Daizhou were mobilized; following Xu Ding's advice, they were kept at Dai to shield Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenyou under Emperor Xuanzong, five thousand garrison troops from Daizhou were mobilized; following Xu Ding's advice, they were retained at Dai to shield Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 興定二年，選募河南、陝西弩手軍二千人為一軍，賜號威勇。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xingding, two thousand crossbowmen were selected and recruited from Henan and Shaanxi as one army, granted the designation Awesome Courage.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xingding, two thousand crossbowmen were selected and recruited from Henan and Shaanxi as a single army and granted the designation Awesome Courage.

sentences.zh: 及南遷，河北封九公，因其兵假以便宜從事，沿河諸城置行樞密院元帥府，大者有「便宜」之號，小者有「從宜」之名。

translations.literal: When the court moved south, nine dukes were enfeoffed in Hebei and their troops were granted discretionary authority; along the river cities Mobile Privy Councils and Marshal Prefectures were established—the larger with the title "discretionary," the smaller with the name "as appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: After the southern relocation, nine dukes were enfeoffed in Hebei and their troops granted discretionary authority; Mobile Privy Councils and Marshal Prefectures were established in cities along the river—the larger styled "discretionary," the smaller "as appropriate."

sentences.zh: 元光間，時招義軍以三十人為謀克， 五謀克為一千戶，四千戶為一萬戶，四萬戶為一副統，兩副統為一都統，此複國初之名也。

translations.literal: During Yuanguang, volunteer armies were recruited with thirty men as a mouke, five mouke as a qianhu, four thousand qianhu as a wanhu, forty thousand wanhu as a deputy chief commander, and two deputy chief commanders as a chief commander—this revived the names of the founding era.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanguang, volunteer armies were organized with thirty men to a mouke, five mouke to a qianhu, four thousand qianhu to a wanhu, forty thousand wanhu to a deputy chief commander, and two deputy chief commanders to a chief commander—reviving the nomenclature of the founding era.

sentences.zh: 然又外設一總領提控，故時皆稱元帥為總領雲。

translations.literal: Yet an outer chief controller was also established, so at the time all called the marshal "chief controller."
translations.idiomatic: An additional chief controller was also placed above the command structure, so that marshals were commonly addressed as "chief controller."

sentences.zh: 金初因遼諸抹而置群牧，抹之為言無蚊蚋、美水草之地也。

translations.literal: At the founding of the Jin, herd administrations were established following the Liao mo pastures; mo means land without mosquitoes and gnats and with fine water and grass.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Jin, herd administrations were established on the model of the Liao mo pastures; mo denoted land free of mosquitoes and gnats and rich in water and grass.

sentences.zh: 天德間，置迪河斡朵、斡裏保保亦作本、蒲速裏、燕恩、兀者五群牧所，皆仍遼舊名，各設官以治之。

translations.literal: During Tiande, five herd administrations were established: Dihe Woduo, Woli Baobao—also written Ben—Pusuli, Yan'en, and Wuzhe, all retaining old Liao names, each with officials to administer them.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiande five herd administrations were established—Dihe Woduo, Woli Baobao (also written Ben), Pusuli, Yan'en, and Wuzhe—all retaining old Liao names, each with its own staff of officials.

sentences.zh: 又于諸色人內，選家富丁多，及品官家子、猛安謀克蒲輦軍與司吏家余丁及奴，使之司牧，謂之「群子」，分牧馬駝牛羊，為之立蕃息衰耗之刑賞。

translations.literal: From among men of all categories, those with wealthy households and many sons, sons of ranked officials, pulian troops of meng'an and mouke, surplus sons of clerks' households, and slaves were chosen to manage the herds; they were called "herd boys," tending horses, camels, cattle, and sheep separately, with rewards and punishments established for increase and loss.
translations.idiomatic: From among all classes of people the court chose wealthy households with many sons, sons of ranked officials, pulian troops of meng'an and mouke, surplus sons from clerks' households, and slaves to manage the herds. Called "herd boys," they tended horses, camels, cattle, and sheep by assignment, under regulations rewarding increase and punishing loss.

sentences.zh: 後稍增其數為九。

translations.literal: Later the number was gradually increased to nine.
translations.idiomatic: Later the number was gradually increased to nine.

sentences.zh: 契丹之亂遂亡其五，四所之所存者馬千余、牛二百八十餘、羊八百六十、駝九十而已。

translations.literal: The Khitan rebellion then destroyed five of them; of the four that remained there were only a little over a thousand horses, more than two hundred eighty cattle, eight hundred sixty sheep, and ninety camels.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan rebellion destroyed five of the administrations; of the four that survived there remained only a little over a thousand horses, some two hundred eighty cattle, eight hundred sixty sheep, and ninety camels.

sentences.zh: 世宗置所七：曰特滿、忒滿在撫州、斡睹只、蒲速碗、蒲速碗本斡睹只之地，大定七年分其地置之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong established seven offices: Teman and Tetman at Fuzhou; Woduzhi; Pusuwan—Pusuwan was originally Woduzhi's territory, and in the seventh year of Dading its land was divided to establish it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong established seven offices: Teman and Tetman at Fuzhou; Woduzhi; and Pusuwan—the last carved out of Woduzhi's territory in the seventh year of Dading.

sentences.zh: 承安三年改為板底因烏魯古。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chengan it was renamed Bandi Yin Wulugu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chengan it was renamed Bandi Yin Wulugu.

sentences.zh: 甌裏本、承安三年改為烏鮮烏魯古。

translations.literal: Ouliben—in the third year of Chengan renamed Wuxian Wulugu.
translations.idiomatic: Ouliben was renamed Wuxian Wulugu in the third year of Chengan.

sentences.zh: 烏魯古者言滋息也。

translations.literal: Wulugu means to breed and multiply.
translations.idiomatic: Wulugu means "to breed and multiply."

sentences.zh: 合魯碗、耶盧碗。

translations.literal: Heluwan and Yelüwan.
translations.idiomatic: Heluwan and Yelüwan.

sentences.zh: 在武平縣、臨潢、泰州之境。

translations.literal: They lay in Wuping County and the territories of Linhuang and Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: They lay within Wuping County and the territories of Linhuang and Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 大定二十年三月，更定群牧官、詳穩脫朵、知把、群牧人滋息損耗賞罰格。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twentieth year of Dading, the offices of herd administration, xiangwen tuoduo, zhiba, and the regulations for rewards and punishments when herd keepers increased or lost livestock were re-fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twentieth year of Dading, herd offices were reorganized and regulations governing rewards and punishments for increases and losses in livestock were revised.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，敕諸所，馬三歲者付女直人牧之，牛或以借民耕，或又令民畜羊，或以賑貧戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, an edict ordered the various offices: horses aged three years were handed to Jurchen people to herd; cattle were sometimes lent to civilians for farming, or civilians were ordered to raise sheep, or livestock was used to relieve poor households.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year an edict ordered that three-year-old horses be entrusted to Jurchen herders; cattle were sometimes lent to civilians for farming, sheep were sometimes assigned to commoners to raise, and livestock was sometimes distributed to relieve poor households.

sentences.zh: 時遣使閱實其數，缺則杖其官，而令牧人償之，匿其實者監察舉覺之。

translations.literal: At the time envoys were sent to inspect and verify the numbers; when there were shortfalls the officials were beaten with the staff, herd keepers were made to compensate, and those who concealed the true count were detected when censors reported them.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were dispatched to inspect and verify herd counts. Shortfalls brought beating for the responsible officials and forced compensation from the herders; anyone who concealed the true numbers was exposed when censors investigated.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，蕃息之久，馬至四十七萬，牛十三萬，羊八十七萬，駝四千。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, after long breeding and increase, horses reached four hundred seventy thousand, cattle one hundred thirty thousand, sheep eight hundred seventy thousand, and camels four thousand.
translations.idiomatic: By the twenty-eighth year, after years of steady increase, the herds had grown to four hundred seventy thousand horses, one hundred thirty thousand cattle, eight hundred seventy thousand sheep, and four thousand camels.

sentences.zh: 明昌五年，散騬馬，令中都、西京、河北東、西路驗民物力分畜之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Mingchang, gelded horses were distributed; the Central Capital, Western Capital, and Hebei East and West circuits were ordered to assess civilian wealth and allocate the animals for raising.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Mingchang era, the court distributed gelded horses and ordered the Central Capital, Western Capital, and Hebei East and West circuits to assess civilian wealth and assign the animals for raising.

sentences.zh: 又令它路民養馬者，死則于前四路所養者給換，若欲用則悉以送官。

translations.literal: It was further ordered that civilians raising horses in other circuits, when a horse died, would receive a replacement from those raised in the aforesaid four circuits; if they wished to use the horses, all were to be sent to the government.
translations.idiomatic: Civilians in other circuits who raised horses were further ordered that when a horse died they would receive a replacement from stock raised in those four circuits, and that if they wished to put the animals to use they must surrender them all to the government.

sentences.zh: 此金之馬政也。

translations.literal: Such was the Jin horse policy.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the Jin dynasty's horse policy.

sentences.zh: 然每有大役，必括於民，及取群官之餘騎，以供戰士焉。

translations.literal: Yet whenever there was a major campaign, horses were inevitably requisitioned from the people, and surplus mounts from herd offices were taken to supply the fighting troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever a major campaign arose, the state inevitably requisitioned horses from the people and drew surplus mounts from herd offices to equip the fighting troops.

sentences.zh: 宣宗興定元年，定民間收潰軍亡馬之法，及以馬送官酬直之格：「上等馬一匹銀五十兩，中下遞減十兩。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingding under Emperor Xuanzong, regulations were fixed for civilians receiving horses lost by routed armies, and scales for turning horses in to the government for payment: "For a horse of the upper grade, fifty taels of silver per horse; middle and lower grades decreasing by ten taels each."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xingding era under Emperor Xuanzong, the court fixed regulations for civilians who recovered horses lost by routed armies and scales for surrendering horses to the government in exchange for payment: an upper-grade horse was worth fifty taels of silver, with middle and lower grades decreasing by ten taels each.

sentences.zh: 不願酬直者，上等二匹補一官，雜班任使，中等三匹，下等四匹，如之。

translations.literal: Those unwilling to accept payment: two upper-grade horses would earn one office appointment, assignable among the miscellaneous ranks; three middle-grade horses, four lower-grade horses—the same rule applied.
translations.idiomatic: Those who declined payment could turn in two upper-grade horses for appointment to a miscellaneous-rank office; three middle-grade horses or four lower-grade horses earned the same reward.

sentences.zh: 令下十日陳首，限外匿及殺，並絞。

translations.literal: After the order was issued, ten days were allowed for voluntary disclosure; concealing after the deadline or killing horses—all were punished by strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Once the order was promulgated, ten days were allowed for voluntary disclosure; concealment after the deadline, or killing a horse, was punishable by strangulation.

sentences.zh: 」又遣官括市民馬，立賞格以示勸，五百匹以上鈔千貫，千匹以上一官，二千匹以上兩官。

translations.literal: " Officials were also sent to requisition horses from city commoners, with reward scales established to encourage compliance: one thousand strings of paper money for five hundred horses or more; one office for one thousand horses or more; two offices for two thousand horses or more.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were also dispatched to requisition horses from urban commoners, with reward scales set to encourage compliance: one thousand strings of paper money for five hundred horses or more, one office for one thousand or more, and two offices for two thousand or more.

sentences.zh: 養兵之法

translations.literal: Methods for Maintaining Troops
translations.idiomatic: Methods for Training Troops.

sentences.zh: 熙宗天眷三年正月，詔歲給遼東戍卒綢絹有差。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Tianjuan under Emperor Xizong, an edict ordered annual allotments of silk and gauze to garrison troops in Eastern Liao in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of the Tianjuan era under Emperor Xizong, an edict ordered graded annual allotments of silk and gauze for garrison troops in Eastern Liao.

sentences.zh: 正隆四年，命河南、陝西統軍司並虞候司順德軍，官兵並增廩給。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenlong, the Henan and Shaanxi frontier command headquarters and the Shunde Army of the yuhou office were ordered to increase grain rations for officers and troops alike.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Zhenlong era, the Henan and Shaanxi frontier command headquarters and the Shunde Army under the yuhou office were ordered to increase grain rations for both officers and rank-and-file troops.

sentences.zh: 六年，將南征，以絹萬匹于京城易衣襖穿膝一萬，以給軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, preparing for the southern campaign, ten thousand bolts of silk were exchanged in the capital for ten thousand padded jackets with knee-length skirts to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, as the southern campaign was prepared, ten thousand bolts of silk were exchanged in the capital for ten thousand padded jackets with knee-length skirts to equip the army.

sentences.zh: 世宗大定三年，南征，軍士每歲可支一千萬貫，官府止有二百萬貫，外可取於官民戶，此軍須錢之所由起也。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dading under Emperor Shizong, during the southern campaign, troops required ten million strings per year but the government had only two million; the remainder had to be taken from official and civilian households—this was the origin of military expense monies.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Dading era under Emperor Shizong, the southern campaign required ten million strings of cash each year while the government treasury held only two million; the rest had to be levied from official and civilian households. Thus began the system of military expense funds.

sentences.zh: 時言事者，以山東、河南、陝西等路循宋、齊舊例，州縣司吏、弓手於民間驗物力均敷顧錢，名曰「免役」，請以是錢贍軍。

translations.literal: At the time memorialists noted that Shandong, Henan, Shaanxi, and other circuits followed Song and Qi precedents whereby prefectural and county clerks and archers assessed civilian wealth and levied averaged support monies called "exemption from corvée"; they asked that these funds support the army.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists at the time noted that Shandong, Henan, Shaanxi, and other circuits followed Song and Qi precedents under which prefectural and county clerks and archers assessed civilian wealth and levied averaged support payments called "exemption from corvée," and they proposed that these funds be used to support the army.

sentences.zh: 至是，省具數以聞，詔罷弓手錢，其司吏錢仍舊。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Secretariat submitted the figures and memorialized; an edict abolished the archers' levy, while clerks' monies remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat thereupon submitted the figures and memorialized the throne; an edict abolished the archers' levy while leaving the clerks' payments unchanged.

sentences.zh: 四年六月，奏，元帥府乞降軍須錢，上曰：「帥府支費無度，例皆科取於民，甚非朕意。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year, a memorial reported that the Marshal's Headquarters requested military expense funds; the Emperor said: "The marshal's office spends without limit and habitually levies from the people—this is far from my intent."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourth year, a memorial reported that the Marshal's Headquarters was seeking military expense funds. The emperor said, "The marshal's office spends without restraint and habitually levies the people—this is far from what I intend."

sentences.zh: 仰會計軍須支用不盡之數，及諸路轉運司見在如實缺用，則別具以聞。

translations.literal: "First account for unspent military funds and what the various route transport offices currently hold; if there is a genuine shortfall, report separately."
translations.idiomatic: First account for unspent military funds and what the route transport offices currently hold; if there is a genuine shortfall, report it separately.

sentences.zh: 」十年四月，命德順州建營屋以處屯軍。

translations.literal: " In the fourth month of the tenth year, orders were issued to build barracks at Deshun Prefecture to house garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the tenth year, the court ordered barracks built at Deshun Prefecture to quarter garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 十七年七月，歲以羊皮三萬賜西北路戍兵。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the seventeenth year, thirty thousand sheepskins were granted annually to garrison troops on the Northwestern Route.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the seventeenth year, thirty thousand sheepskins were granted each year to garrison troops on the Northwestern Route.

sentences.zh: 承安三年，以軍須所費甚大，乞驗天下物力均征。

translations.literal: In the third year of Cheng'an, because military expenses were very great, a request was made to assess wealth throughout the empire and levy a uniform tax.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Cheng'an era, because military expenses had grown very heavy, officials requested a nationwide assessment of wealth and a uniform levy.

sentences.zh: 擬依黃河夫錢例，征軍須錢，驗各路新籍物力，每貫征錢四貫，西京、北京、遼東路每貫征錢二貫，臨潢、全州則免征，周年三限送納。

translations.literal: It was proposed to follow the Yellow River corvée-money precedent and levy military expense monies according to newly registered wealth in each route: four strings per registered string, two strings in the Western Capital, Northern Capital, and Eastern Liaoning routes; exempt in Linhuang and Quanzhou; payment in three installments over the year.
translations.idiomatic: It was proposed to follow the Yellow River corvée-money precedent and levy military expense funds according to newly registered wealth in each circuit: four strings of cash for every registered string, two strings in the Western Capital, Northern Capital, and Eastern Liaoning circuits, exemption in Linhuang and Quanzhou, and payment in three installments over the year.

sentences.zh: 恐期遠，遂定制作半年三限輸納。

translations.literal: Fearing the term was too long, it was fixed that collection begin within half a year in three installments.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the payment period was too long, the court fixed collection to begin within half a year, payable in three installments.

sentences.zh: 凡河南、陝西、山東放老千戶、謀克、蒲輦、正軍、阿裏喜等給賞之例，舊軍千戶十年以上賞銀五十兩、絹三十匹，不及十年，比附十年以上謀克支。

translations.literal: For Henan, Shaanxi, and Shandong, regulations for grants when discharging old thousand-commanders, mouke, pulian, regular soldiers, alixi, and the like: veteran thousand-commanders of ten years or more received fifty taels of silver and thirty bolts of silk; less than ten years were paid at the mouke rate for ten years or more.
translations.idiomatic: In Henan, Shaanxi, and Shandong, discharge grants for veteran thousand-commanders, mouke, pulian, regular soldiers, alixi, and the like were fixed as follows: thousand-commanders with ten or more years of service received fifty taels of silver and thirty bolts of silk; those with less than ten years were paid at the rate for mouke of ten years or more.

sentences.zh: 謀克十年以上銀四十兩，絹二十五匹，不及十年銀三十兩、絹二十匹。

translations.literal: Mouke of ten years or more: forty taels of silver and twenty-five bolts of silk; less than ten years: thirty taels and twenty bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Mouke with ten or more years of service received forty taels of silver and twenty-five bolts of silk; those with less than ten years received thirty taels and twenty bolts.

sentences.zh: 蒲輦十年以上銀三十兩，絹二十匹，不及十年銀二十兩，絹一十五匹。

translations.literal: Pulian of ten years or more: thirty taels of silver and twenty bolts of silk; less than ten years: twenty taels and fifteen bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Pulian with ten or more years of service received thirty taels of silver and twenty bolts of silk; those with less than ten years received twenty taels and fifteen bolts.

sentences.zh: 馬步正軍、阿裏喜等勾當不拘年分，放老正軍銀一十五兩、絹一十匹，阿裏喜、旗鼓、吹笛、本司火頭人等同銀八兩、絹五匹。

translations.literal: Cavalry and infantry regular soldiers, alixi, and those on duty without regard to years of service: discharged regular soldiers received fifteen taels of silver and ten bolts of silk; alixi, banner-drummers, flute-players, and fire-keepers of the bureau alike received eight taels and five bolts.
translations.idiomatic: For cavalry and infantry regulars, alixi, and men on active duty without regard to length of service, discharged regular soldiers received fifteen taels of silver and ten bolts of silk; alixi, banner-drummers, flute-players, and bureau fire-keepers alike received eight taels and five bolts.

sentences.zh: 三虞候千戶，十年以上銀四十兩，絹二十五匹。

translations.literal: Yuhou thousand-commanders of ten years or more: forty taels of silver and twenty-five bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Yuhou thousand-commanders with ten or more years of service received forty taels of silver and twenty-five bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 不及十年銀三十兩、絹二十匹。

translations.literal: Less than ten years: thirty taels of silver and twenty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Those with less than ten years received thirty taels of silver and twenty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 謀克二十年以上銀五十兩、絹三十匹，十年以上銀三十兩、絹二十匹，不及十年銀一十兩、絹一十五匹。

translations.literal: Mouke of twenty years or more: fifty taels of silver and thirty bolts of silk; ten years or more: thirty taels and twenty bolts; less than ten years: ten taels and fifteen bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Mouke with twenty or more years of service received fifty taels of silver and thirty bolts of silk; those with ten or more years received thirty taels and twenty bolts; those with less than ten years received ten taels and fifteen bolts.

sentences.zh: 蒲輦十年以上銀二十兩、絹一十五匹，不及十年銀一十五兩、絹一十匹。

translations.literal: Pulian of ten years or more: twenty taels of silver and fifteen bolts of silk; less than ten years: fifteen taels and ten bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Pulian with ten or more years of service received twenty taels of silver and fifteen bolts of silk; those with less than ten years received fifteen taels and ten bolts.

sentences.zh: 正軍、阿裏喜、勾當不拘年分，放老正軍銀一十兩、絹七匹，阿裏喜、旗鼓、吹笛、本司火頭人等同銀五兩，絹四匹。

translations.literal: Regular soldiers, alixi, and those on duty without regard to years of service: discharged regular soldiers received ten taels of silver and seven bolts of silk; alixi, banner-drummers, flute-players, and fire-keepers of the bureau alike received five taels and four bolts.
translations.idiomatic: For regular soldiers, alixi, and men on active duty without regard to length of service, discharged regular soldiers received ten taels of silver and seven bolts of silk; alixi, banner-drummers, flute-players, and bureau fire-keepers alike received five taels and four bolts.

sentences.zh: 北邊萬戶、千戶、謀克等，曆過軍功及年老放罷給賞之例遷官同從吏部格，正千戶管押萬戶，勾當過一十五年，遷兩官與從五品。

translations.literal: Northern frontier ten-thousand-commanders, thousand-commanders, mouke, and the like: regulations for grants and office advancement upon accumulated merit and old-age discharge followed the Ministry of Personnel standards; formal thousand-commanders supervising ten-thousand-commanders, after fifteen years of service, were promoted two ranks to Associate Fifth Grade.
translations.idiomatic: For northern frontier ten-thousand-commanders, thousand-commanders, mouke, and the like, discharge grants and promotions for accumulated military merit and old-age release followed Ministry of Personnel regulations: formal thousand-commanders who had supervised ten-thousand-commanders for fifteen years were promoted two ranks to Associate Fifth Grade.

sentences.zh: 不及一十五年年老放罷，遷一官與正六品。

translations.literal: Less than fifteen years at old-age discharge: one promotion to Regular Sixth Grade.
translations.idiomatic: Those discharged for age with less than fifteen years of service received one promotion to Regular Sixth Grade.

sentences.zh: 若十年以下，遷一官賞銀絹六十兩匹。

translations.literal: If under ten years: one promotion and a reward of sixty taels of silver and bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Those with less than ten years received one promotion and a reward of sixty taels of silver and bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 正謀克管押萬戶，勾當一十五年遷兩官與正六品，不及一十五年年老放罷，遷一官與正七品，若十年以下遷一官賞銀絹五十兩匹。

translations.literal: Formal mouke supervising ten-thousand-commanders: fifteen years of service earned two promotions to Regular Sixth Grade; less than fifteen years at old-age discharge earned one promotion to Regular Seventh Grade; under ten years earned one promotion and a reward of fifty taels of silver and bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Formal mouke who supervised ten-thousand-commanders were promoted two ranks to Regular Sixth Grade after fifteen years of service; those discharged for age with less than fifteen years received one promotion to Regular Seventh Grade; those with less than ten years received one promotion and a reward of fifty taels of silver and bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 正千戶官押千戶，勾當過二十年，遷一官與正六品，不及二十年年老放罷，遷一官與正七品，若十年以下遷一官賞銀絹四十兩匹。

translations.literal: Formal thousand-commanders supervising thousand-commanders: over twenty years of service earned one promotion to Regular Sixth Grade; less than twenty years at old-age discharge earned one promotion to Regular Seventh Grade; under ten years earned one promotion and a reward of forty taels of silver and bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Formal thousand-commanders who supervised thousand-commanders were promoted one rank to Regular Sixth Grade after more than twenty years of service; those discharged for age with less than twenty years received one promotion to Regular Seventh Grade; those with less than ten years received one promotion and a reward of forty taels of silver and bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 正謀克管押千戶以下，依河南、陝西體例。

translations.literal: Formal mouke supervising thousand-commanders and below followed the Henan and Shaanxi precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Formal mouke who supervised thousand-commanders and below followed the Henan and Shaanxi precedents.

sentences.zh: 凡鎮防軍，每年試射，射若有出眾，上等賞銀四兩，特異眾者賞十兩銀馬盂。

translations.literal: For frontier garrison troops, annual archery trials were held; outstanding performance earned four taels of silver for the upper grade, and exceptional performers received ten taels and a silver horse cup.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier garrison troops held annual archery trials: outstanding marksmen of the upper grade received four taels of silver, and those whose skill was truly exceptional received ten taels and a silver horse cup.

sentences.zh: 簽充武衛軍，挈家赴京者，人日給六口糧，馬四匹芻槁。

translations.literal: Those drafted into the Imperial Guard who brought their families to the capital received six persons' grain ration per day and fodder for four horses.
translations.idiomatic: Men drafted into the Imperial Guard who brought their families to the capital received daily grain rations for six persons and fodder for four horses.

sentences.zh: 諸招軍月給例物。

translations.literal: Monthly standard allotments for recruited troops.
translations.idiomatic: Standard monthly allotments for recruited troops.

sentences.zh: 邊鋪軍錢五十貫、絹十匹。

translations.literal: Border post troops: fifty strings of cash and ten bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Border post troops received fifty strings of cash and ten bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 軍匠上中等錢五十貫、絹五匹，下等錢四十貫、絹四匹。

translations.literal: Military artisans of upper and middle grade: fifty strings of cash and five bolts of silk; lower grade: forty strings and four bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Military artisans of upper and middle grade received fifty strings of cash and five bolts of silk; those of lower grade received forty strings and four bolts.

sentences.zh: 黃河埽兵錢三十貫、絹五匹，射糧軍及溝渠等處埽兵水手，錢二十貫、絹二匹，士兵錢十貫、絹一匹。

translations.literal: Yellow River dike troops: thirty strings of cash and five bolts of silk; grain-transport archers and dike troops and sailors at canals and the like: twenty strings and two bolts; soldier-farmers: ten strings and one bolt.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow River dike troops received thirty strings of cash and five bolts of silk; grain-transport archers and dike troops and sailors at canals and similar posts received twenty strings and two bolts; soldier-farmers received ten strings and one bolt.

sentences.zh: 凡射糧軍指揮使及黃、沁埽兵指揮使，錢粟七貫石、絹六匹，軍使錢粟六貫石、絹同上，什將錢二貫、粟三石，春衣錢五貫、秋衣錢十貫。

translations.literal: Grain-transport archer commanders and Yellow and Qin dike commanders: seven strings of cash and seven shi of grain and six bolts of silk; army commissioners six strings and six shi, silk the same; squad leaders two strings and three shi of grain; spring clothing five strings, autumn clothing ten strings.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders of grain-transport archers and of Yellow and Qin dike troops received seven strings of cash, seven shi of grain, and six bolts of silk; army commissioners received six strings and six shi with the same silk allotment; squad leaders received two strings and three shi of grain; spring clothing cost five strings and autumn clothing ten strings.

sentences.zh: 承局押官錢一貫五百文、粟二石，春衣錢五貫、秋衣錢七貫。

translations.literal: Clerks and escort officers: one string five hundred cash and two shi of grain; spring clothing five strings, autumn clothing seven strings.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks and escort officers received one string five hundred cash and two shi of grain; spring clothing five strings and autumn clothing seven strings.

sentences.zh: 牢城並士兵錢八百文、粟二石，春衣錢四貫、秋衣錢六貫。

translations.literal: Penal troops and soldier-farmers: eight hundred cash and two shi of grain; spring clothing four strings, autumn clothing six strings.
translations.idiomatic: Penal troops and soldier-farmers received eight hundred cash and two shi of grain; spring clothing four strings and autumn clothing six strings.

sentences.zh: 邊鋪軍請給與射糧軍同。

translations.literal: Border post troops received the same allowances as grain-transport archers.
translations.idiomatic: Border post troops received the same allowances as grain-transport archers.

sentences.zh: 河南、陝西、山東路統軍司鎮防甲軍、馬軍，猛安錢八貫、米五石二斗、絹八匹、六馬芻粟，謀克錢六貫、米二石八斗、絹六匹、五馬芻粟，蒲輦錢四貫、米石七斗、絹五匹、四馬芻粟，正軍錢二貫、米石五斗、絹四匹、綿十五兩、兩馬芻粟，阿裏喜錢一貫五百文、米七斗、絹三匹、綿十兩。

translations.literal: For armored and cavalry garrison troops under the Henan, Shaanxi, and Shandong frontier command headquarters: meng'an received eight strings of cash, five shi two dou of rice, eight bolts of silk, and fodder for six horses; mouke six strings, two shi eight dou, six bolts, and fodder for five horses; pulian four strings, one shi seven dou, five bolts, and fodder for four horses; regular soldiers two strings, one shi five dou, four bolts, fifteen liang of cotton, and fodder for two horses; alixi one string five hundred cash, seven dou of rice, three bolts of silk, and ten liang of cotton.
translations.idiomatic: Armored and cavalry garrison troops under the Henan, Shaanxi, and Shandong frontier commands were paid as follows: meng'an received eight strings of cash, five shi two dou of rice, eight bolts of silk, and fodder for six horses; mouke six strings, two shi eight dou, six bolts, and fodder for five horses; pulian four strings, one shi seven dou, five bolts, and fodder for four horses; regular soldiers two strings, one shi five dou, four bolts, fifteen liang of cotton, and fodder for two horses; alixi one string five hundred cash, seven dou of rice, three bolts of silk, and ten liang of cotton.

sentences.zh: 步軍，猛安馬二匹、謀克馬一匹芻粟。

translations.literal: For infantry, meng'an received fodder for two horses and mouke for one.
translations.idiomatic: Infantry meng'an received fodder for two horses and mouke for one.

sentences.zh: 每馬給芻一束、粟五升，歲仲青野有青草馬可收養則止，惟每猛安當差馬七十二匹，四時皆給。

translations.literal: Each horse received one bundle of fodder and five sheng of grain; in midsummer when pasture had green grass and horses could graze, payment stopped, except for seventy-two horses on duty per meng'an, which were supplied in all four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Each horse received one bundle of fodder and five sheng of grain. In midsummer, when open pasture provided green grass and horses could graze, payments ceased—except for the seventy-two horses on active duty per meng'an, which received fodder in all four seasons.

sentences.zh: 又定制河南、山東、河東歲給五月，陝西六月。

translations.literal: It was further fixed that Henan, Shandong, and Hedong were paid in the fifth month and Shaanxi in the sixth.
translations.idiomatic: The court further fixed fifth-month payment for Henan, Shandong, and Hedong and sixth-month payment for Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 鎮防軍補買馬錢，河南路正軍五百文，阿裏喜隨色人三百文，陝西、山東路正軍三百文，阿裏喜隨色人二百文。

translations.literal: Garrison horse replacement monies: on the Henan route regular soldiers received five hundred cash and alixi and attendants three hundred; on the Shaanxi and Shandong routes regular soldiers received three hundred cash and alixi and attendants two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Horse replacement allowances for garrison troops were set at five hundred cash for regular soldiers and three hundred for alixi and attendants on the Henan circuit; on the Shaanxi and Shandong circuits regular soldiers received three hundred cash and alixi and attendants two hundred.

sentences.zh: 諸屯田被差及緣邊駐紮捉殺軍，猛安月給錢六貫、米一石八斗、五馬芻粟，謀克錢四貫、米一石二斗、三馬芻粟，蒲輦錢二貫、米六斗、二馬芻粟，正軍錢一貫五百文、米四斗、一馬芻粟，阿裏喜隨色人錢一貫、米四斗、一馬芻粟。

translations.literal: Military colonists on assignment and frontier garrison troops stationed for pursuit and suppression: meng'an received monthly six strings of cash, one shi eight dou of rice, and fodder for five horses; mouke four strings, one shi two dou, and fodder for three horses; pulian two strings, six dou, and fodder for two horses; regular soldiers one string five hundred cash, four dou, and fodder for one horse; alixi and attendants one string, four dou, and fodder for one horse.
translations.idiomatic: Military colonists on assignment and frontier troops stationed for pursuit and suppression were paid monthly as follows: meng'an six strings of cash, one shi eight dou of rice, and fodder for five horses; mouke four strings, one shi two dou, and fodder for three horses; pulian two strings, six dou, and fodder for two horses; regular soldiers one string five hundred cash, four dou, and fodder for one horse; alixi and attendants one string, four dou, and fodder for one horse.

sentences.zh: 德順軍指揮使錢六貫、米二石八斗、絹六匹、三馬芻粟，軍使什將錢四貫、米一石七斗、絹五匹，給兩馬料，長行錢二貫、米一石五斗、絹四匹、綿十五兩，給一馬料，奚軍謀克錢一貫五百文、米一石五斗、綢絹春秋各一匹，給三馬料，蒲輦錢一貫、米二石七斗、綢絹同上，給二馬料，長行錢一貫、米一石八斗、綢絹同上，飼一馬。

translations.literal: The Deshun Army commander received six strings of cash, two shi eight dou of rice, six bolts of silk, and fodder for three horses; army commissioners and squad leaders four strings, one shi seven dou, five bolts of silk, and fodder for two horses; rank-and-file soldiers two strings, one shi five dou, four bolts of silk, fifteen liang of cotton, and fodder for one horse; Xi army mouke one string five hundred cash, one shi five dou of rice, one bolt each of silk and gauze for spring and autumn, and fodder for three horses; pulian one string, two shi seven dou, the same silk and gauze, and fodder for two horses; rank-and-file soldiers one string, one shi eight dou, the same silk and gauze, and fodder for one horse.
translations.idiomatic: The commander of the Deshun Army received six strings of cash, two shi eight dou of rice, six bolts of silk, and fodder for three horses. Army commissioners and squad leaders received four strings, one shi seven dou, five bolts of silk, and fodder for two horses. Rank-and-file soldiers received two strings, one shi five dou, four bolts of silk, fifteen liang of cotton, and fodder for one horse. Xi army mouke received one string five hundred cash, one shi five dou of rice, one bolt each of silk and gauze for spring and autumn, and fodder for three horses. Pulian received one string, two shi seven dou, the same silk and gauze allotment, and fodder for two horses. Rank-and-file soldiers received one string, one shi eight dou, the same silk and gauze, and fodder for one horse.

sentences.zh: 北邊臨潢等處永屯駐軍，千戶錢八貫、米五石二斗、絹八匹、飼馬六匹，步軍飼兩馬、地五頃，謀克錢六貫、米二石八斗、絹六匹、飼五馬、地四頃，蒲輦錢四貫、米一石七斗、絹五匹、飼四馬、地三頃，正軍錢二貫、米一石四斗五升、絹四匹、綿十五兩、飼兩馬、地二頃，阿裏喜錢一貫五百文、米七斗、絹三匹、綿十兩、地一頃，旗鼓司人與阿裏喜同，交替軍錢二貫、米四斗，阿裏喜錢一貫五百文、米四斗。

translations.literal: Permanent garrison troops at Linhuang and other northern posts: thousand-commanders received eight strings of cash, five shi two dou of rice, eight bolts of silk, and fodder for six horses; infantry received fodder for two horses and five qing of land; mouke six strings, two shi eight dou, six bolts of silk, fodder for five horses, and four qing of land; pulian four strings, one shi seven dou, five bolts of silk, fodder for four horses, and three qing; regular soldiers two strings, one shi four dou five sheng, four bolts of silk, fifteen liang of cotton, fodder for two horses, and two qing; alixi one string five hundred cash, seven dou of rice, three bolts of silk, ten liang of cotton, and one qing of land; banner-office personnel the same as alixi; rotation troops two strings and four dou of rice; rotation alixi one string five hundred cash and four dou.
translations.idiomatic: Permanent garrison troops at Linhuang and other northern posts were paid as follows: thousand-commanders eight strings of cash, five shi two dou of rice, eight bolts of silk, and fodder for six horses; infantry received fodder for two horses and five qing of land; mouke six strings, two shi eight dou, six bolts of silk, fodder for five horses, and four qing; pulian four strings, one shi seven dou, five bolts of silk, fodder for four horses, and three qing; regular soldiers two strings, one shi four dou five sheng, four bolts of silk, fifteen liang of cotton, fodder for two horses, and two qing; alixi one string five hundred cash, seven dou of rice, three bolts of silk, ten liang of cotton, and one qing; banner-office personnel the same as alixi; rotation troops two strings and four dou of rice; rotation alixi one string five hundred cash and four dou.

sentences.zh: 上番漢軍，千戶月給錢三貫、糧四石、絹八匹、飼四馬，謀克錢二貫五百文、糧一石、絹六匹、飼二馬，正軍錢二貫、米九斗五升、絹四匹。

translations.literal: Han troops on upper rotation: thousand-commanders received monthly three strings of cash, four shi of grain, eight bolts of silk, and fodder for four horses; mouke two strings five hundred cash, one shi of grain, six bolts of silk, and fodder for two horses; regular soldiers two strings, nine dou five sheng of rice, and four bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Han troops serving upper rotation received monthly pay as follows: thousand-commanders three strings of cash, four shi of grain, eight bolts of silk, and fodder for four horses; mouke two strings five hundred cash, one shi of grain, six bolts of silk, and fodder for two horses; regular soldiers two strings, nine dou five sheng of rice, and four bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 上京路永屯駐軍所除授，千戶月給錢粟十五貫石、絹十匹、綿二十兩、飼 三馬，謀克錢六貫、米二石八斗、絹六匹、飼二馬，正軍月支錢二貫五百文、米一石二斗、絹四匹、綿十五兩、飼一馬，阿裏喜隨色人錢二貫、米一石二斗，絹四匹、綿十五兩。

translations.literal: For permanent garrison appointments on the Upper Capital route: thousand-commanders received monthly fifteen strings of cash and shi of grain, ten bolts of silk, twenty liang of cotton, and fodder for three horses; mouke six strings, two shi eight dou, six bolts of silk, and fodder for two horses; regular soldiers two strings five hundred cash, one shi two dou, four bolts of silk, fifteen liang of cotton, and fodder for one horse; alixi and attendants two strings, one shi two dou, four bolts of silk, and fifteen liang of cotton.
translations.idiomatic: Permanent garrison appointments on the Upper Capital circuit were paid monthly as follows: thousand-commanders fifteen strings of cash and shi of grain, ten bolts of silk, twenty liang of cotton, and fodder for three horses; mouke six strings, two shi eight dou, six bolts of silk, and fodder for two horses; regular soldiers two strings five hundred cash, one shi two dou, four bolts of silk, fifteen liang of cotton, and fodder for one horse; alixi and attendants two strings, one shi two dou, four bolts of silk, and fifteen liang of cotton.

sentences.zh: 諸北邊永駐軍，月給補買馬錢四百文，隨色人三百文。

translations.literal: All northern permanent garrison troops received monthly horse replacement monies of four hundred cash, and attendants three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: All permanent garrison troops in the north received monthly horse replacement allowances of four hundred cash; attendants received three hundred.

sentences.zh: 貞祐三年，軍前委差及掌軍官，規圖糧料，冒占職役，皆無實員，又見職及遙授者，已有俸給，又與無職事者同支券糧，故時議欲省員減所給之數，俟征行則全給之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyou, field-assigned officers and army commanders schemed over grain rations, falsely occupying posts without actual personnel; incumbents and remotely appointed men who already received salaries also drew ration coupons like men without offices, so opinion at the time favored reducing posts and cutting allotments, with full payment restored only when troops took the field.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Zhenyou era, officers assigned to the front and army commanders manipulated grain rations and held posts in name only without actual personnel. Incumbents and remotely appointed officials who already drew salaries also received ration coupons like men without offices, so contemporary opinion favored reducing posts and cutting payments, restoring full allotments only when troops marched to war.

sentences.zh: 及興定二年，彰化軍節度使張行信言：「一軍充役，舉家廩給，蓋欲感悅士心，使為國盡力耳！

translations.literal: By the second year of Xingding, Zhang Xingxin, military commissioner of the Zhanghua Army, said: "When one soldier serves, the whole household receives rations—the intent is to win soldiers' hearts and make them exert themselves for the state!"
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Xingding era, Zhang Xingxin, military commissioner of the Zhanghua Army, said, "When one soldier enters service, his whole household receives rations. The purpose is to win the troops' loyalty and move them to give their all for the state!"

sentences.zh: 至於無軍之家，複無丁男，而其妻女猶受給何謂耶？

translations.literal: As for households with no soldier and no adult men, yet whose wives and daughters still receive rations—what can this mean?
translations.idiomatic: But what are we to make of households with no soldier and no adult men, whose wives and daughters still receive rations?

sentences.zh: 」五年，京南行三司官石抹斡魯言：「京南、東、西三路見屯軍戶，老幼四十萬口，歲費糧百四十余萬石，皆坐食民租，甚非善計。

translations.literal: " In the fifth year, Shi Mo Wolu, official of the Southern Capital branch of the Three Offices, said: "In the Southern, Eastern, and Western Capital circuits, registered garrison households counting old and young total four hundred thousand mouths; grain costs exceed one million four hundred thousand shi annually—all living off civilian rent. This is a poor plan indeed."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Shi Mo Wolu, an official of the Southern Capital branch of the Three Offices, said, "In the Southern, Eastern, and Western Capital circuits, registered garrison households—including old and young—number four hundred thousand mouths and consume more than 1.4 million shi of grain each year, all of it drawn from civilian rent. This is a poor policy indeed."

sentences.zh: 」語在《田制》。

translations.literal: " The account is in the Treatise on Land.
translations.idiomatic: The account is recorded in the Treatise on Land.

sentences.zh: 諸屯田軍人，如差防送，日給錢一百五十文。

translations.literal: Military colonists assigned to escort duty received one hundred fifty cash per day.
translations.idiomatic: Military colonists assigned to escort duty received one hundred fifty cash per day.

sentences.zh: 看管孝甯宮人，月各給米五斗、柴一車、春秋衣粗布一段、秋絹二匹、綿一十五兩。

translations.literal: Custodians of Xiaoning Palace personnel received monthly five dou of rice, one cart of firewood, one length of coarse cloth for spring and autumn clothing, two bolts of autumn silk, and fifteen liang of cotton.
translations.idiomatic: Custodians of Xiaoning Palace personnel received each month five dou of rice, one cart of firewood, one length of coarse cloth for spring and autumn clothing, two bolts of autumn silk, and fifteen liang of cotton.

sentences.zh: 諸黃院子年滿者，以元請錢糧三分內，給一貫石養老。

translations.literal: Yellow Yard personnel upon completing their term received one string and one shi from within one-third of their original allotted pay for retirement support.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Yard personnel who completed their term of service received one string of cash and one shi of grain from one-third of their original allotment as a retirement allowance.
